x: Total receipts for 2023-24 were revised from ₹2,78,302 crore (BE) to ₹2,50,000 crore (RE), a cut of about 10.2%. (These are total receipts; revenue receipts proper were ₹1,73,767 crore in 2023-24.)

In 2024-25 RE (revenue receipts ₹1,91,142 crore), own tax revenue of ₹94,967 crore was about half (~48%), central transfers of ₹89,157 crore about 45-47%, and own non-tax revenue of ₹7,018 crore only about 4%, the smallest. Only C keeps this order and these approximate shares.

The 128% jump is partly a low-base effect: agriculture and allied was budgeted at Rs. 12,514 crore in 2024-25 but the RE was only Rs. 6,192 crore (about 51% underspent), so growth to Rs. 14,138 crore in 2025-26 BE looks large. C states the opposite (high base).

Under MGNREGA the Centre bore 100% of unskilled wages; its replacement, the VB-G RAM G Act, uses a 60:40 Centre-State pattern for most States, raising State contributions. NFSA concerns food grains, PM-KISAN is a Central Sector scheme and NRLM is a livelihoods mission, none of which replaced MGNREGA.

Fishing and aquaculture was the fastest-growing agriculture sub-sector in 2025-26 at 17.69%. Construction, the fastest in industry, grew 14.18% (not 15.13%), and communications grew about 15.28% (Survey overview), not 17.69%.

In April-October 2025, CPI-IW inflation was 1.86% in Andhra Pradesh against 2.82% for India, even though AP's Combined CPI index level was higher (200.6 vs 195.9). C reverses the figures and D attaches them to CPI-AL rather than CPI-IW.
SES 2025-26 has 11 chapters, from General Overview and Swarna Andhra @2047 Vision through Public Finance, Social Infrastructure and Poverty/Employment to the last one, Data-Driven Governance.
AP ranks 8th in India by GSDP (Feb 2026 report). Note 8th is also AP's rank by area; its population-share rank is 10th.

APSES 2024-25 reported 3,863 ward secretariats. 8,489 is the number of functional Rythu Seva Kendras, 9,018 the MEPMA slum-level federations and 2,740 is a distractor echoing the 2.74 lakh urban SHGs.
The 2nd Advance Estimates put 2025-26 foodgrain output at 190.29 lakh tonnes (kharif 110.00 + rabi 80.29 lakh t, up 17.03%). 47.28 lakh tonnes is fisheries output up to December 2025.
Fish production of 47.28 lakh tonnes up to December 2025 was 72% of the annual target. 17.03% is the rise in foodgrain output and 84.47 relates to lakh women in rural SHGs.
8,489 RSKs were functional after rationalisation. The Survey's 10,778 and 10,606 figures refer to RSKs providing soil sampling and animal husbandry services; 3,863 is the count of ward secretariats.
Tax devolution to States contracted 19.5% in Q1 2026-27, and the new non-shareable HSNS cess may shrink the divisible pool further.
The 2026-27 BE puts outstanding debt at ₹7,11,094 crore, about 36% of GSDP. ₹6,35,177 crore was 2025-26 RE and ₹5,64,488 crore 2024-25 RE.

AP has 26 districts and a 974 km coastline, which ranks 2nd longest in India. The 'third-longest' ranking goes with the remeasured length of 1,053 km, not 974 km, so C mixes the two measurements; A has the wrong district count and D the wrong length.
key: The notes give AP's coastline as 974 km = 2nd longest; 3rd longest applies only to the remeasured 1,053 km. AP has 26 districts.
